mainTopic: How an ox becomes a מועד: רבי מאיר's קל וחומר and the זבה challenge, the rulings of רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון, and whether the three days are about the ox or the owner
overview: רבי מאיר argues with a קל וחומר. If an ox that gores on spread-out days becomes a מועד, then one that gores three times close together should become one even more. The רבנן push back from the case of a זבה, where spread-out sightings make her טמאה but close-together ones do not. רבי מאיר answers that the word וזאת makes זב and זבה a special rule set by the פסוק: a זב is counted by sightings and a זבה by days. The גמרא then works out why the פסוק is read this way, using a היקש of male to female and the context of the passage. Next, a ברייתא brings two more views. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון each mix the opinions of רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר on becoming a מועד and on going back to תם. רב נחמן rules like רבי יוסי, because his reasoning is sound. Finally, the גמרא asks whether רבי יהודה's three days are meant to make the ox a מועד or to warn the owner. It brings a ברייתא about three sets of lying witnesses to test the question, and the analysis continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's argument: gorings close together are even worse
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר argues with a קל וחומר. If gorings spread out over days make the owner liable as a מועד, then gorings close together should do so all the more.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the ox spaced out its gorings, the owner is liable. If it goes close together, isn't it obvious that he is liable?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר gives a logical argument that an ox goring three times close together, even on one day, becomes a מועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that three gorings on separate days make an ox a מועד. רבי מאיר says gorings packed close together show an even stronger habit of goring. So by logic they should certainly count.

keyTerms.meaning: spaced out, spread apart
brought close together
gorings
isn't it all the more so?

steps.whyThisMatters: This קל וחומר is the claim that the rest of the passage tests.

phrases.english: If it spaced out its gorings — he is liable;
phrases.notes: This means three gorings on three different days, which makes the ox a מועד, so the owner pays full damages.

phrases.english: if it brought its gorings close together, is it not all the more so?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of how an ox becomes a מועד, giving רבי מאיר's reasoning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ox that gores three times close together becomes a מועד, by קל וחומר from gorings spread over days.

steps.title: The רבנן challenge from the case of זבה
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן bring a counter-example. A זבה becomes טמאה when her sightings are spread over days, but not when they are close together, so 'closer' is not always 'stronger'.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: a זבה proves otherwise. When her sightings are spread out, she is טמאה. When they are close together, she is טהורה!
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן attack רבי מאיר's קל וחומר with a case where spread-out events count but close-together ones do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if 'close together' is always more severe. With a זבה, three sightings on three days make her a זבה, but three sightings on one day do not. That breaks the logic of 'all the more so'.

keyTerms.meaning: a woman with a flow of blood outside her normal time, who becomes טמאה as a זבה
will prove (that the argument fails)
sightings of a flow
ritually impure / ritually pure

phrases.english: They said to him: a זבה will prove otherwise,
for if she spaced out her sightings, she is impure,
phrases.notes: This means three sightings on three days in a row, which makes her a full זבה.

phrases.english: if she brought her sightings close together, she is pure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks רבי מאיר's קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's קל וחומר that close-together gorings are more severe
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A counter-example: for a זבה, spread-out sightings make her טמאה but close-together ones do not, so 'closer' does not mean 'stronger'.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: the פסוק makes זב and זבה a special rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר answers that the word וזאת in the פסוק sets a special rule. A זב is counted by sightings, and a זבה by days. So her case cannot be used to defeat logic elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: the פסוק says, 'And this shall be his impurity in his flow.' The פסוק made the זב depend on sightings and the זבה depend on days.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר defends his קל וחומר by showing that the זבה rule comes from a special פסוק, not from logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וזאת ('and this') tells us to follow the פסוק exactly as written. For a זבה, the תורה chose days, even though logic would not lead there. Since this is a rule from a פסוק, it does not prove anything about oxen. So the קל וחומר still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'and this', a word that limits the rule to exactly what is written
a man with an unusual discharge who becomes טמא
the פסוק made it depend on
days

steps.whyThisMatters: A rule set by a פסוק against normal logic cannot be used to knock down a קל וחומר in a different area.

phrases.english: He said to them: behold, it says:
"And this shall be his impurity in his flow" —
the verse made the זב depend on sightings,
and the זבה depend on days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רבנן's challenge from זבה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the counter-example is a rule set by a פסוק, not by logic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The זבה case shows that close-together events can be weaker, which would defeat the קל וחומר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The זבה rule comes from the word וזאת, which sets זב by sightings and זבה by days. So it does not defeat a קל וחומר about oxen.

steps.title: Maybe the word excludes the man from days instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know וזאת removes the זבה from counting by sightings. Maybe it removes the זב from counting by days.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know this 'and this' comes to exclude a זבה from sightings? Say instead it comes to exclude a זב from days!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבי מאיר's reading of the פסוק and suggests the opposite direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וזאת is written about the זב. So maybe it limits him: only sightings count for him, and sightings on separate days do not. If so, nothing teaches that the זבה is limited to days.

keyTerms.meaning: from where (do we know)?
to exclude
say instead

phrases.english: From where do we know that this "and this" —
comes to exclude a זבה from being counted by sightings?
Say instead it comes to exclude a זב from being counted by days!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how רבי מאיר read the פסוק in his answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's reading that וזאת excludes זבה from counting by sightings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word could just as well limit the זב, so that he is counted only by sightings on one day and not by days.

steps.title: The verse compares male to female, so a man also counts by days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a היקש. A פסוק puts male and female together, so just as a female counts by days, a male also counts by days. So וזאת cannot be removing the זב from days.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, 'And the one with a flow, whether male or female.' It compares male to female: just as a female is counted by days, so too a male is counted by days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves from another פסוק that a זב can also be counted by days, which rules out the suggestion in step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the פסוק lists זכר and נקבה together, we learn one from the other through a היקש. Since a female is counted by days, a male is too. So וזאת must be teaching something else: that a זבה is not counted by sightings.

keyTerms.meaning: the פסוק says
compares through a היקש, learning one thing from another written next to it
male / female

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר קְרָא: ״וְהַזָּב אֶת זוֹבוֹ לַזָּכָר וְלַנְּקֵבָה״ –
phrases.english: The verse says: "And the one with a flow, whether male or female" —
it compares male to female;

phrases.aramaic: מָה נְקֵבָה בְּיָמִים, אַף זָכָר בְּיָמִים.
phrases.english: just as a female is counted by days, so too a male is counted by days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: וְהַזָּב אֶת זוֹבוֹ לַזָּכָר וְלַנְּקֵבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from a היקש in another פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: וזאת might remove the זב from being counted by days.
steps.terutzMaskana: The היקש shows a זב is counted by days too, so וזאת must instead remove the זבה from being counted by sightings.

steps.title: Why not compare female to male instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the היקש should not run the other way: just as a male is counted by sightings, a female should be too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us compare female to male: just as a male is counted by sightings, so too a female should be counted by sightings!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the היקש, saying the comparison could point in the opposite direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A היקש links the two cases, but it does not say which one teaches the other. If the female learns from the male, then three sightings on one day would make a woman a זבה. That would bring back the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: but let him compare (the other way)

phrases.english: But let it compare female to male —

phrases.aramaic: מָה זָכָר בִּרְאִיּוֹת, אַף נְקֵבָה בִּרְאִיּוֹת!
phrases.english: just as a male is counted by sightings, so too a female is counted by sightings!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the direction of the היקש from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The direction of the היקש between זכר and נקבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The comparison could go the other way, making a female counted by sightings like a male.

steps.title: The word וזאת blocks the reverse comparison
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תורה already excluded this with the word וזאת. A female is not counted by sightings, so the היקש can only teach that the male also counts by days.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the Merciful One already excluded this with 'and this'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The word וזאת stops a זבה from being counted by sightings, so the היקש can only go from female to male.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each source does its own job. וזאת limits the זבה to days. The היקש adds days for the זב. Together they confirm רבי מאיר's answer: the זבה rule is a decree of the פסוק, so his קל וחומר about oxen stands.

keyTerms.meaning: but the Merciful One (the תורה) already excluded it

steps.whatToRemember: זב: counted by sightings, and by the היקש also by days. זבה: counted only by days, because of וזאת. Since this rule comes from a פסוק, the זבה case does not defeat רבי מאיר's קל וחומר.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two sources. וזאת is what keeps a זבה from counting by sightings. The היקש only adds that a זב can also count by days.

phrases.english: But the Merciful One excluded this with "and this."
phrases.notes: Since וזאת already rules out sightings for a woman, the comparison can only work in one direction: female teaching male.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6. Step 8 then asks why וזאת is read this way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing to a limiting word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The היקש could make a female counted by sightings like a male.
steps.terutzMaskana: וזאת already excludes a female from sightings, so the היקש only teaches that a male also counts by days.

steps.title: Why Choose That Reading of the Word
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reason we have to say וזאת takes the זבה out of counting by sightings, rather than taking the זב out of counting by days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see to choose this reading?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a reason. Two readings of וזאת seemed possible, so why did we pick one over the other?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 5-7 built on the idea that וזאת removes counting by sightings from the זבה. But the word could have been read the other way, as removing counting by days from the זב. The גמרא wants to know what tips the balance.

keyTerms.meaning: And what did you see? A request for the reason behind a choice.

phrases.english: And what did you see?
phrases.notes: He means: why read וזאת as limiting the woman's sightings, and not the man's days?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the reading of וזאת that step 7 relied on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that וזאת excludes the זבה from counting by sightings.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both readings seem equally possible, so choosing one needs a reason.

steps.title: The Verse Is About Sightings, So It Limits Sightings
steps.stepSummary: It makes sense that a word placed in a passage about sightings is limiting sightings, not days.
steps.simpleTranslation: It stands to reason. The passage is dealing with sightings, so it limits sightings. Would it be dealing with sightings and then limit days?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the context decides. The word וזאת appears in a passage that talks about sightings, so it must be limiting sightings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The section of the זב counts by sightings and does not mention days. A limiting word placed in that section should limit what the section is talking about, which is sightings. Reading it as limiting days would pull in a topic the passage never raised.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason; it makes sense.
It is standing in, meaning it is dealing with this topic.
It limits or excludes something.
Sightings, the times a discharge is seen.

steps.whatToRemember: A limiting word in a פסוק limits the subject that the פסוק is already talking about.

phrases.english: It stands to reason:
it is dealing with sightings, so it limits sightings;
would it be dealing with sightings and limit days?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: וזאת could just as easily limit days for the זב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the passage deals with sightings, וזאת limits sightings. This means the זבה is not counted by sightings.

steps.title: Two More Views on מועד and תם
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי יוסי says an ox becomes a מועד through goring on three days, and goes back to תם when children pet it and it does not gore. רבי שמעון says it becomes a מועד through goring three times, and the three days are only for going back.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Which ox is a מועד? Any ox that witnesses testified about on three days. And it is a תם again once children pet it and it does not gore. These are the words of רבי יוסי. רבי שמעון says: A מועד is any ox that witnesses testified about three times, and the three days were said only for going back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the goring ox from the משנה. It brings a ברייתא with two new opinions on how an ox becomes a מועד and how it returns to תם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה said a מועד needs goring on three days, and returning to תם takes three days without goring. רבי מאיר said a מועד needs three gorings, and it is a תם again once children pet it and it does not gore. רבי יוסי takes רבי יהודה's view on מועד and רבי מאיר's view on תם. רבי שמעון does the reverse.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; this opens a ברייתא.
A forewarned ox, one known to gore, whose owner pays full damage.
An ox not known to gore, whose owner pays half damage.
Touching or petting.
Going back, here meaning the ox returning to being a תם.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון each agree with רבי יהודה on one question and with רבי מאיר on the other, but in opposite ways. A simple chart helps: רבי יוסי = יהודה for מועד and מאיר for תם. רבי שמעון = מאיר for מועד and יהודה for תם.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Which ox is a forewarned one?
Any ox that witnesses testified about, that it gored on three days;
and it is innocuous again when children pet it
and it does not gore;
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei.
Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: מוּעָד – כֹּל שֶׁהֵעִידוּ בּוֹ שָׁלֹשׁ פְּעָמִים,
phrases.english: A forewarned ox is any ox that witnesses testified gored three times,
and they did not speak of three days
except for going back alone.
phrases.notes: Going back means the ox becomes a תם again, which takes three days without goring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the זב and זבה side topic and goes back to the topic of מועד and תם from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: מועד = gored on three days; תם = children pet it and it does not gore. רבי שמעון: מועד = gored three times; going back to תם = three days.

steps.title: רב נחמן Rules Like the Parts רבי יוסי Agrees With
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רב אדא בר אהבה, rules like רבי יהודה on מועד and like רבי מאיר on תם, because רבי יוסי agrees with each of them on that point.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רב אדא בר אהבה: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה about מועד, since רבי יוסי agrees with him. And the הלכה follows רבי מאיר about תם, since רבי יוסי agrees with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives the practical ruling. On each question he picks the opinion that has רבי יוסי's support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On each question there is a dispute, and רב נחמן uses a third תנא to decide it. On מועד, רבי יוסי sides with רבי יהודה (three days). On תם, he sides with רבי מאיר (children pet it and it does not gore).

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the opinion of...
Agrees with him.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda concerning forewarned,
since Rabbi Yosei agrees with him;
and the halakha follows Rabbi Meir concerning innocuous,
since Rabbi Yosei agrees with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּמוּעָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical ruling based on the ברייתא in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מועד = gored on three days (like רבי יהודה). Back to תם = children pet it and it does not gore (like רבי מאיר).

steps.title: רבא: Why Not Follow רבי שמעון's Agreement Instead
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן why he doesn't rule the other way, like רבי מאיר on מועד and like רבי יהודה on תם, since רבי שמעון agrees with each of them on those points.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: Let the Master say the הלכה follows רבי מאיר about מועד, since רבי שמעון agrees with him. And the הלכה follows רבי יהודה about תם, since רבי שמעון agrees with him!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges the ruling. The same kind of reasoning, using רבי שמעון's support instead, would give the opposite result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן decided each question by seeing which side a third תנא supports. But there are two such תנאים, and רבי שמעון supports the opposite side on both questions. So 'a third תנא agrees' does not settle anything by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: And let the Master say; a challenge proposing a different ruling.

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Naḥman:

phrases.aramaic: וְלֵימָא מָר הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּמוּעָד,
phrases.english: And let the Master say the halakha follows Rabbi Meir concerning forewarned,
since Rabbi Shimon agrees with him;
and the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda concerning innocuous,
since Rabbi Shimon agrees with him!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן: וְלֵימָא מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning behind רב נחמן's ruling in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's method of deciding by רבי יוסי's agreement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון's agreement points the opposite way on both questions, so the method could support either ruling.

steps.title: רב נחמן: I Follow רבי יוסי, Whose Reasoning Is Sound
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that he simply holds like רבי יוסי, because רבי יוסי's reasoning is sound.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I hold like רבי יוסי, because רבי יוסי's reasoning is with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן explains that his ruling really comes from following רבי יוסי himself. It does not come from counting who agrees with whom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two 'agreements' cancel each other out, so רב נחמן needs a reason to prefer one תנא. He prefers רבי יוסי, because there is a known principle that רבי יוסי's reasoning is solid. So the הלכה follows רבי יוסי's full position: three days for מועד, and children petting it without goring for תם.

keyTerms.meaning: I hold; this is my view.
His reasoning is with him, meaning his logic is sound and well-founded.

steps.whatToRemember: The final ruling follows רבי יוסי: an ox becomes a מועד by goring on three days, and becomes a תם again when children pet it and it does not gore.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a principle for deciding הלכה: רבי יוסי's opinion carries special weight, because his reasoning is considered sound.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I hold in accordance with Rabbi Yosei,
as Rabbi Yosei's reasoning is with him.
phrases.notes: Literally 'his reason is with him.' It means his rulings are well thought out and reliable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי סְבִירָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the real basis of the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling depends on which side the other תנאים support, so רבי שמעון's support could reverse it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling comes from following רבי יוסי, whose reasoning is sound, so רבי שמעון's support does not change it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי: מועד after goring on three days, and תם again when children pet it and it does not gore.

steps.title: Are the three days about the ox or about the owner?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יהודה's 'three days' are meant to make the ox a מועד or to warn the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: the 'three days' the משנה mentions, are they there to make the ox a מועד, or to warn the man who owns it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about what the 'three days' in רבי יהודה's view are really for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One option is that the three days are about the ox: they show it has a real habit of goring. The other option is that they are about the owner: he must be warned properly so he knows to guard his ox. The גמרא wants to know which one is the real reason.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before them (the חכמים had a real doubt)
To make the ox a מועד (a known gorer)
To warn the man (the owner)

steps.confusionAlert: The word לייעודי is used both ways here. With the ox it means 'to make it a מועד.' With the man it means 'to warn him.' It is the same root (עד, witness or warning) used in two senses.

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
The "three days" that the משנה teaches,
are they to make the ox a מועד,
or to warn the man?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ruling like רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה on מועד, the גמרא now asks what the three-day requirement is fundamentally about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the three days are needed to establish the ox's nature or to give the owner proper warning.

steps.title: The practical difference: three sets of witnesses on one day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the question matters when three sets of witnesses testify on one day about three gorings on three different days.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make? When three groups of witnesses come on one day. If you say the days are to make the ox a מועד, it is a מועד. If you say they are to warn the man, it is not a מועד, because the owner can say: 'Only now are they testifying against me.' So what is the answer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows a real case where the two sides of the question give different results, and then asks again what the answer is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ox really gored on three separate days, but all the witnesses came to court on a single day. If the days are about the ox, its pattern is proven and it is a מועד. If the days are about warning the owner, he got all his warnings on one day, so the ox is not yet a מועד.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?
Groups (sets) of witnesses
It becomes a מועד
He can say (the owner has an argument)

phrases.english: What practical difference does it make?
When three groups of witnesses came
on one day.
If you say it is to make the ox a מועד, it is a מועד;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ לְיַיעוֹדֵי גַּבְרָא, לָא מִיַּיעַד –
phrases.english: but if you say it is to warn the man, it is not a מועד,
because he can say:
"It is only now that they are testifying against me."
So what is the answer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sharpens the question from step 14 by giving a case where the two options lead to different rulings.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete case that separates 'making the ox a מועד' from 'warning the owner', followed by a renewed request for the answer.

steps.title: A ברייתא: testimony must be before the owner and the court
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא saying an ox only becomes a מועד when the witnesses testify in front of both the owner and בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: An ox does not become a מועד until witnesses testify about it in front of the owner and in front of בית דין. If they testified in front of בית דין but not the owner, or in front of the owner but not בית דין, it does not become a מועד until they testify in front of both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts bringing a ברייתא to try to answer the question. This is the first part of the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא requires the testimony to be given in front of both the owner and בית דין. This opening is background. The line the גמרא actually builds on is the next one, about three sets of witnesses and הזמה (steps 17-20).

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a source is being brought to answer a question)
In front of the owner
In front of the court

phrases.english: Come and hear:
An ox does not become a מועד
until witnesses testify about it
in front of the owner and in front of בית דין.
If they testified about it in front of בית דין
but not in front of the owner,

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְנֵי בְעָלִים וְשֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי בֵית דִּין –
phrases.english: or in front of the owner but not in front of בית דין,
it does not become a מועד

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיָּעִידוּ בּוֹ בִּפְנֵי בֵית דִּין וּבִפְנֵי בְעָלִים.
phrases.english: until they testify about it in front of בית דין and in front of the owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins an attempt to answer the question raised in steps 14 and 15 using a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The question of whether the three days are about the ox or about warning the owner.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא requiring testimony in front of both the owner and בית דין for an ox to become a מועד.

steps.title: Three sets of witnesses count as one testimony for הזמה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: three pairs of witnesses for three gorings are three testimonies, but they count as one testimony for הזמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If two witnesses testified about the first goring, two about the second, and two about the third, there are three testimonies here, but they count as one testimony for הזמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues quoting the same ברייתא. This second part is the line that touches our case of three groups of witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each pair testifies about a separate goring, so there are three separate testimonies. But the ברייתא says that for הזמה, the punishment of lying witnesses, all three pairs are treated as one unit. That is because only all three together make the ox a מועד, and this is what the גמרא will build on.

keyTerms.meaning: Testimonies
One testimony (treated as a single unit)
Proving witnesses to be lying witnesses (עדים זוממין), which brings a punishment on them

steps.whyThisMatters: This line deals with three separate groups of witnesses, just like the case in step 15. That is why the גמרא brings it to answer the question.

phrases.english: If two testified about it regarding the first goring,
and two regarding the second,
and two regarding the third,
there are three testimonies here,
but they count as one testimony for הזמה.
phrases.notes: הזמה is when other witnesses prove these witnesses could not have seen what they claimed, so the lying witnesses are punished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא from step 16, adding the rule about three sets of witnesses and הזמה.
steps.raayaObject: Whether three groups of witnesses about three gorings make the ox a מועד, as in the case of step 15.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's ruling that three pairs of witnesses are three testimonies but one testimony for הזמה.

steps.title: If the first or second set is shown to be lying, everyone is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains what happens if the first set, or the first two sets, of witnesses are found to be זוממין. The owner is exempt, and so are the witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the first set is found to be זוממין, two testimonies are left. The owner is exempt and the witnesses are exempt. If the second set is also found to be זוממין, one testimony is left. Again the owner is exempt and the witnesses are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going. It walks through what happens as the witness sets are shown to be זוממין one at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the first set falls away, only two gorings are proven. That is not enough to make the ox a מועד, so the owner does not pay full damages. The lying witnesses also pay nothing, because without the other sets their testimony alone could never have made him pay full damages. The same is true once the second set also falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: A set (a pair) of witnesses
Is found to be lying witnesses (זוממין)
Testimonies
Exempt, does not have to pay

steps.confusionAlert: 'He is exempt' does not mean the owner pays nothing at all. The gorings that are still proven make him pay half damages, as for any ox that is not a מועד. He is only exempt from the full damages a מועד would owe.

phrases.english: If the first set is found to be lying witnesses,
there are two testimonies left here,
and he is exempt, and they are exempt.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the owner, who doesn't pay full damages. 'They' are the lying witnesses, who don't have to pay him anything.

phrases.english: If the second set is found to be lying witnesses,
there is one testimony left here,
and he is exempt, and they are exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from Step 17. It applies the rule that the three sets count as one testimony for הזמה.
steps.raayaObject: The question from Step 14: are the three days meant to make the ox a מועד, or to warn the owner?
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about three sets of witnesses testifying about three gorings

steps.title: If the third set is also shown to be lying, all of them are liable
steps.stepSummary: Once the third set is also found to be זוממין, all three sets must pay. The source is the פסוק 'וַעֲשִׂיתֶם לוֹ כַּאֲשֶׁר זָמַם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the third set is found to be זוממין, all of them are liable. About this the פסוק says: 'And you shall do to him as he plotted to do.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its case. When all three sets turn out to be lying, all three are punished together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Together, the three sets were trying to make the ox a מועד, which would have forced the owner to pay full damages. So they are treated as one testimony and all share the payment. This is the 'one testimony for הזמה' rule from Step 17 put into practice.

keyTerms.meaning: All of them
Liable, they must pay
'Do to him as he plotted to do': the פסוק that is the source for punishing עדים זוממין

steps.whatToRemember: Lying witnesses who together tried to make an ox a מועד are punished only when all three sets are shown to be lying. Then all of them pay together.
steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא will use this ruling, that even the first set is liable, to test the two ways of reading רבי יהודה's 'three days'.

phrases.english: If the third set is found to be lying witnesses,
all of them are liable.
And about this it is said:
'And you shall do to him as he plotted, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: נִמְצֵאת כַּת שְׁלִישִׁית זוֹמֶמֶת – כּוּלָּן חַיָּיבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the case begun in Step 18. Once all three sets are shown to be lying, liability falls on all of them.
steps.raayaObject: The question from Step 14: are the three days meant to make the ox a מועד, or to warn the owner?
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's ruling that all three sets are liable, based on דברים 19:19

steps.title: This ruling fits well if the three days are meant to make the ox a מועד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to analyze the ברייתא. If the three days are meant to make the ox a מועד, the ruling that all sets are liable makes sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the three days are to make the ox a מועד, that works out well.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now uses the ברייתא to answer its question from Step 14. Here it gives the first half: one reading fits nicely. This sets up the next move, which will check the other reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the goal is to make the ox a מועד, all three sets can come on the same day and know about each other. That makes them partners in one effort, so even the first set can fairly be held liable. The unspoken question is whether the 'warn the owner' reading can explain this ruling too.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say
To make (the ox) a מועד
The ox
It works out well, it fits

steps.confusionAlert: 'שַׁפִּיר' is only half of the argument. The גמרא is about to ask what happens under the other reading, so this is not yet the final answer.

phrases.english: If you say it is to make the ox a forewarned one, it works out well.
phrases.notes: 'It' means רבי יהודה's three days from Step 14.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the ברייתא's ruling from Step 19 and applies it to the question raised in Steps 14-15.
steps.raayaObject: The view that the three days are meant to make the ox a מועד
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's ruling that even the first set is liable when all three sets are shown to be lying
